successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: the Gowa-Tallo core (Cliopatria's 1662 outline) without the Fort Rotterdam and Somba Opu cells that the VOC took in 1667 and 1669

ledger.x: 1320: Gowa is established on the Makassar coast.

c. 1512: Gowa and Tallo are reunified. 'During the reign of King of Gowa X, Tunipalangga (1512-1546), the two kingdoms were reunified'; the page gives a reign span, not a year, so the year is Cliopatria's first (1512). Disagreement: the Tallo Kingdom page (opened 2026-10-19) puts the Gowa-Tallo power-sharing agreement…
1548: the capital moves from Tamalate to the fortress of Somba Opu (infobox: Tamalate 1320-1548, Somba Opu 1548-1670).
22 September 1605: Gowa-Tallo becomes a sultanate.
1611: Gowa invades Bone.
1611: Bone accepts Islam, 'the last major Bugis kingdom to accept Islam, in 1611' (Bone page); 'By 1611 all southwest Sulawesi, including Makassar's Bugis rival Bone, had become Muslim' (Gowa page).
1618: Makassar attacks Sumbawa.
1626: the third expedition.
1626: Sumbawa under Makassar.
1644: Bone rises against Gowa.
April-May 1646: Bone is defeated at Passempe.
1646: Gowa installs a regent over Bone.
1660: a Bugis revolt.
1660: the revolt is 'ultimately crushed' and Palakka flees South Sulawesi; the page gives no month, so the contest is closed the same year.
1666: the Makassar War begins.
1667: Bone escapes Gowa.
1667: Makassar loses Sumbawa.
18 November 1667: Gowa becomes a vassal of the VOC.
18 November 1667: the Treaty of Bongaya cedes Jum Pandan to the VOC.
June 1669: Somba Opu falls.
June 1669: the VOC takes the Somba Opu coast.
1670: the seat moves from Somba Opu to Kalegowa (infobox: Kalegowa 1670-1680, 1692-1702 and 1753-1895; Hasanuddin resigned in 1669 and died on 12 June 1670).
31 December 1799: the VOC is dissolved.
1800: Gowa's overlord is the Dutch East Indies.
1911: Gowa loses its independence.
1911: the vassal sultanate becomes a Dutch East Indies regency.
1911: the Sultanate of Gowa ends as a state.

wars.name: Makassar War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Bongaya (18 November 1667) reduced Gowa to a VOC vassal and ceded Jum Pandan; Hasanuddin renewed the war and lost Somba Opu in June 1669; Bone, with the VOC, replaced Gowa as the leading South Sulawesi state.

wars.name: Gowa's expeditions against Sumbawa
wars.outcome: Three expeditions (1618, 1619, 1626) overcame Salisi's resistance; a Makassarese-backed ruler was installed and a rebellion of 1632-33 was beaten down; suzerainty over Sumbawa ended with the VOC's victories of 1667/1669.

wars.name: Gowa's wars with Bone
wars.outcome: Gowa invaded Bone in 1611 and forced its conversion; Bone rose in 1644 and was defeated at Passempe (April-May 1646), after which Gowa installed a regent; the Bugis revolt of 1660 under Arung Palakka was crushed; Bone's king was restored in 1667.

wars.name: Dutch South Sulawesi expedition against Gowa
wars.outcome: Gowa lost its independence in 1911 and became a regency of the Dutch East Indies.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty fixes Gowa's frontier; the Treaty of Bongaya of 1667 names Jum Pandan (the future Fort Rotterdam) and Somba Opu only, and the Dutch vassalage that followed fixed no line either.
